text: I am Vesk, a scholar. These cellars are older than the town, older than anything. Bring me what you find down there, and the past will pay for itself.
I keep the graves at the mouth of the hill. If you find old things down there, things that hum, do not bring them up. Lay them in the sealed niches. Each floor has one.
A niche in the wall, sealed with old wax and older words. There is room inside for one thing at a time.
Somewhere below, old lamps flare up. Something heavy stirs in the deep.
The niche seals itself with a sigh. The dark grows deeper, and somewhere below, something crumbles to dust.

The hill draws a breath and does not let it out. Lamps burn in halls no one has lit for a thousand years, and the stone guardians stand at every door, waiting for a king. Vesk names himself their steward. Perhaps he will be a better master than the last one. Perhaps the hill will decide.

The hill sleeps. The niches hold what was taken, and the dark below grows quiet and deep. The gravekeeper writes a few more names in her book, and closes it. In town, no one ever learns how close they came.
